chapter: The Latin scene and business of the 1940s-70s
title: Two color lines: Latin and Black
summary: The Latin black orchestra faced double barriers.

story.theme_name: Race and segregation in the jazz life
story.community_name: Segregation on the road and the bandstand

blocks.x: We goto California. When he hit California, the band was such a splash, Bing Crosby tried -- he wanted to do something with us in the picture. He (unintelligible).
I don't know, they were too complex. We were fighting two , Latin and black.
That was a Latin black orchestra. So you're fighting two things.
If it was white and Latin, people look at white, then it would only be one.
Yeah, because at that time there were at least 25 or 30 Latin musicals.

That was my problem, the reason why I got the band was to bridge that. And I thought of -- the day I opened in La Conga nightclub, there was a cafeteria there at 151st and 7,000. (Unintelligible) and they had Latin musicians in there, they wanted to (unintelligible) white. They were making all kinds of money, (unintelligible). So I had to first break that line. I broke that line, I took that Harlem band (unintelligible).
